subject: general
question: The average runs scored by a batsman in 23 matches is 44. In the next 10 matches, the batsman scored an average of 13 runs. Find his average (rounded off to two decimals) in all the 33 matches?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net deviation from the first **average** (44) for the next 10 matches = 10 × (13 − 44) = **−310**.

Distribute this **total deviation** among all 33 matches: −310 ÷ 33 ≈ **−9.39**.

New average = Original Average + Deviation = 44 − 9.39 = **34.61**.

**∴ The correct answer is 34.61.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Matches in 1st set (n₁) = 23, Average (a₁) = 44

Matches in 2ⁿd set (n₂) = 10, Average (a₂) = 13

**Formula Used:**

Combined Average = (n₁ × a₁ + n₂ × a₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0b8125ee5158e0cf151fb6c240207cf96d741526a4294867bed2139da0fb45bd.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total runs in 23 matches = 23 × 44 = **1012**

⇒ Total runs in 10 matches = 10 × 13 = **130**

⇒ Total runs in all 33 matches = 1012 + 130 = **1142**

⇒ Combined Average = 1142 ÷ 33

⇒ Combined Average = 34.60606...

⇒ Rounding off to two decimal places = **34.61**

**∴ The correct answer is 34.61.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Concept

When two groups with different averages are combined, the **resultant average** lies closer to the group with the larger **sample size** (more matches).

Combined Average Formula

Xₐvg = (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂ + ... + nₖxₖ) ÷ (n₁ + n₂ + ... + nₖ), where n is the frequency and x is the value.

Deviation Method for Averages

It involves picking an **assumed mean** and calculating how much the total sum deviates from this mean, then dividing the **net deviation** by the total number of observations.</p
